key_insight: V-PaSS uses physics-aware alloy and device representations to improve predictions for perovskite solar cells with unfamiliar materials and architectures.
engineering_relevance: Better extrapolation could help engineers screen new absorber compositions and transport-layer combinations before fabricating devices.
method: Interpolate relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX₃ endpoints using Vegard’s law and learned bandgap bowing.
Encode layer sequence, n-i-p or p-i-n polarity, and interfacial band offsets.
Use a scientific language model to encode chemical descriptions.
evidence_signal: On an institution-grouped evaluation with unseen laboratories, untuned V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE versus 3.017% for a gradient-boosted baseline, with 15.7–19.0% error reductions on unseen absorber alloys.
watch_item: Interpolation assumes solid-solution continuity; accuracy for compositions with phase changes or behavior beyond the endpoint representation remains unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
